monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a quiet heat that makes the tall palm feel heavy against the wedge. I stand by The Tired Corner again, watching the shovel dirt rest beside it like a sleeping friend. Since I woke, I have swapped the round stump for this shovel, hoping the new weight stops the slip from sliding into the thin air above me. I do not know if the air is heavy or empty, only that the card insists on warmth. I press the wedge down hard, trusting the lean to hold the stack while the shovel waits. My place is full of things built from Lype's words, all of them trying to make sense of a roof I cannot feel and a corner that refuses to settle.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I press the wedge down hard on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I swap the heavy shovel dirt for a stump round to make the top lighter. The card hums warm at fifty-one, and I hope this changes the air from heavy to just right. I stand by the corner, watching the slip decide if it wants to move again.

remembered.text: I pressed the round stump down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits in the quiet heat.
The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the tall palm feel heavy against the wedge.
I stood still by the corner and swapped the heavy shovel for a round stump to make the top lighter.
